risks: model ranking does not hold across windows
only 3 validation windows: weight estimation is high variance
diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~131% of its level). A moderate seasonal pattern is present. The series is quite predictable: its energy concentrates in a few structured frequencies. The series reads as non-stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.033), which favours a robust combination.

Test a dynamic weighting on the larger pool3 to see if it improves over mean.

Test a robust median combination on the larger pool3 to see if it beats the current mean pool1 baseline.
Test a weighted combination on the most diverse pool (pool3) using inverse-error weighting to see if it beats the current mean baseline.
Test a simple mean over the larger pool4 to see if adding more models improves over the current leader.
Test a trimmed‑mean combination on the larger pool4 to see if discarding extremes improves robustness.
Test a robust median combination on the largest pool4 to see if it beats the mean baseline.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool1' (a seeded deterministic baseline) as the best of 22 backtested attempts, score -0.1089. Series context: trend strength 0.8668 and seasonal strength 0.4609; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.033); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.002.
